items.content:
The user wants to clear/delete all local branches except the main branch in a git repository. This is a straightforward shell task.

First, I should check what branches exist and which one is "main". The conventional main branch might be "main" or "master". I should list the branches first to be safe, then delete all local branches except the main branch.

Let me run a command to list branches, then delete the ones that aren't main.

Actually, I can do this in one go with a shell command that lists local branches, excludes main (and maybe HEAD/current), and deletes them.

A safe command would be:
```
git branch | grep -v "^\* main$" | grep -v "^ main$" | xargs git branch -D
```

Or more carefully:
```
git branch --format='%(refname:short)' | grep -v '^main$' | xargs -r git branch -D
```

This deletes all local branches except "main". I should run this. The user gave permission? Well, run_shell requires user permission but the user asked me to do it, so I can proceed. Let me just execute.
